policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'my feet were almost gone' renders either the qere plural verb or the ketiv participle; the English plural follows the subject 'feet' and does not distinguish the verb form. No note on this verse. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV 'My steps had well nigh slipped' is a passive rendering compatible with both the qere plural and the ketiv singular; English number follows 'steps' and does not settle the verb. No note on this verse. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV main text 'his people return hither' renders the qere qal יָשׁוּב (intransitive 'return'); the textual_variant note 'Another reading is, he will bring back his people' is the ketiv hiphil ישיב, explicitly set aside as the alternative.

ASV 'It was too painful for me' uses genderless 'it', which renders qere הוּא or ketiv היא alike; the hebrew_gloss note concerns 'labor in mine eyes' and does not touch the pronoun. Base qere fallback retained.
